author.name: Jannik Aßfalg
credits: repeat98: original 808/909 fixed-point engines and machine integration

presentation.summary: 808 and 909 bassdrum engines; 909 body and transient fitted more closely to private TR-909 direct-out recordings.
presentation.overview: Analog BD synthesizes 808 and 909 bassdrums in the Octatrack DSP. Version 0.1.4 refines the 909 body, Attack and Tune against Skee Mask’s recordings while retaining 808, the shared desk and TDEP/SAT smoothing. Neighboring strength and noise vary subtly; exact transient-shape variation remains approximate.
highlights: 909 harmonic phase/asymmetry and complete-hit envelope/DC fit
Minimum/maximum Attack and final-hit Tune endpoints refined
Direct-out reference comparison at LPF bypass
808, saved controls and existing TDEP/SAT smoothing retained
usage: Assign ANALOG BD in the track machine chooser or SRC SETUP. Double-tap the track to open its engine browser; choose 808 or 909 with UP/DOWN or LEVEL and confirm with YES.
Shape the drum on SRC. The 808 has TONE and SWEEP; the 909 has TUNE and TDEP. Set accent, LPF and desk bands in SRC SETUP; AMP controls track volume.

Switching back to FLEX retains SRC values, so drum settings can cause unexpected STRT, RTRG and RTIM sample playback. Select your sample, open SRC and press SRC + PLAY to initialize the page to Flex defaults; repeat immediately to undo. Check SRC SETUP and the sample assignment afterwards, and review any retained SRC parameter locks, scenes or LFO destinations.

Keep a separate project copy for stock firmware: saving an Analog BD project without this module can clamp its controls. Eight voices do not guarantee enough processing room for every effect combination.

controls.name: PITCH
controls.doc: 808 body pitch; 909 body frequency spans approximately 30–100 Hz.

controls.name: DECAY
controls.doc: Body decay, with a different response for each model.

controls.name: SWEEP / TDEP
controls.doc: 808 pitch excursion; 909 pitch-envelope amount with sample-wise smoothing.

controls.name: SAT
controls.doc: Drive into the shared Mackie desk stage, with smooth table interpolation during modulation.

controls.name: LPF
controls.doc: Output low-pass: OFF at 0, ORIG around 6.57 kHz at 64, 18 kHz at the assignment default 127.

limitations: SPRING REV is excluded from the upstream standalone remix; its shared DARK helper must be restored from local firmware.
Owner reports stable MKII 0.1.3 operation with distinct 808/909 instances and physical persistence. Maximum eight-voice FX load, worst-case chip timing and full memory bounds remain unqualified.
Saving this project on stock firmware can overwrite synth settings.
909 reference uses a decay-modified TR-909 at one recorded decay setting; the full modified range and exact intermediate knob positions are not reproduced.
The direct-out reference excludes the 909 main-out LPF: use LPF 0 for reference comparison; assignment default remains 127.
Neighboring transient shapes remain more consistent than the reference. Current-source physical audio/persistence, maximum FX load, chip timing and complete memory bounds remain unverified.

storage.label: DSP code
storage.conditions: Combined 808/909 glue and engines use 997 P words plus the separate 35-word stock helper. Existing X upload remains 3776 words/core with four 64-word voices; Y/ColdFire allocation unchanged. Complete stack/lifetime bounds remain unmeasured.

processing.label: DSP execution
processing.conditions: Peak 4294/6563 executed instructions per 16-sample block in matched moving-control/min/max/trigger-split tests. 909 mean cost is 6.22% higher than 0.1.3, maximum matched-block increase 6.27%; not chip cycles or full-chain utilization.

impact.conditions: Per active Analog BD voice; both models, control endpoints and trigger splits on both DSP cores. Ratings express relative demand, not chip utilization or maximum FX-load headroom.

cpu.rationale: Existing guarded ColdFire machine/control glue publishes the same saved knob bytes; the smoothing runs entirely in DSP code and adds no ColdFire work.

dsp.rationale: Matched native 909 mean instruction cost rises 6.22% versus 0.1.3, maximum matched block 6.27%, peak 410.1875 instructions/sample. 808 remains bit-identical with unchanged peak 268.375. These are executed instructions, not chip timing.

memory.rationale: 997 P words/core plus the separate 35-word stock helper stay within the donor. The 3776-word X upload/core and four 64-word voices retain their allocations; no extra Y/ColdFire allocation. Complete lifetime/stack bounds remain unmeasured.

tests.summary: 909 body phase/asymmetry, complete envelope/DC and Attack/Tune endpoints fitted to Skee Mask’s direct-out recordings. Native min/max/all128 controls, both-core instance isolation, actual complete-image source/stock AMP output and saved private image round trip pass. Owner accepted AB014REF05 and explicitly waived fresh physical hardware/persistence, worst-case chip timing and complete memory bounds for this exact experimental source. Shape variation remains smaller than in the reference; full FX load and physical persistence remain untested. Historical 0.1.3 MKII results are not relabelled.

tutorial.title: Compare the 909 direct-out response
steps: In a disposable project, hold FUNC and press SRC for SRC SETUP, choose ANALOG BD and press YES. Double-tap the TRACK key, choose 909 and confirm with YES. Set LOW/HIGH to 64 and SAT to 0.

For the direct-out reference, set PITCH 49, DECAY 100, TUNE 0, TDEP 64, ACCNT 72 and LPF 0. Trigger repeated hits at 70 BPM and sweep ATK alone through 0–127, then hold it at one value to hear the small strength/noise differences.

Hold ATK at 0 and sweep TUNE through its endpoints separately. Return SAT to 0 and TDEP to 64, then press STOP and let the tail finish. Choose 808 in the engine browser to compare; its saved knob values remain intact.

steps: Select an audio track with its TRACK key.
Hold FUNC and press SRC to open SRC SETUP. Use DOWN to reach ANALOG BD, then press YES to assign it.
Press SRC to close SETUP and edit the main controls. The 808 model uses PITCH, DECAY, TONE, ATK, SWEEP and SAT; the 909 uses TUNE and TDEP in place of TONE and SWEEP.
Double-tap the assigned track’s TRACK key to open the engine browser. Choose 808 or 909 with UP/DOWN or LEVEL, then press YES. Selecting a model retains the existing knob settings.
Hold FUNC and press SRC for the shared ACCNT, LPF, LOW and HIGH controls. AMP and the track FX pages remain available.
